sb_prompt: DISCUSS PLANNING A FAMILY REUNION.  DRAW ON YOUR EXPERIENCES AND THOSE OF THE OTHER CALLER FOR MAKING THE NEXT GET-TOGETHER SUCCESSFUL AND MEMORABLE.
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!

ParticipantA: Hi, how are you doing today?
ParticipantB: I'm doing well, thanks for asking. How about you?
ParticipantA: I'm doing okay, just had a long day at work. How about you? What do you do for a living?
ParticipantB: I'm a school bus driver. What about you?
ParticipantA: I work as an office receptionist. So, have you ever planned a family reunion before?
ParticipantB: Yeah, I have. My family has a tradition of getting together every couple of years.
ParticipantA: That's great! What makes it memorable for you?
ParticipantB: Well, we usually plan it around a holiday, like Thanksgiving or Christmas. We have a big dinner, exchange gifts, and catch up on each other's lives.
ParticipantA: Sounds lovely. I've never planned a reunion before, but I've always wanted to. My family is spread out all over the country, so it's hard to get everyone together.
ParticipantB: I can imagine. Have you considered using a family reunion planning website?
ParticipantA: No, I haven't. Do you have any recommendations?
ParticipantB: Yes, there's one called "Family Reunion Planner" that I've used before. It's really easy to use and has lots of helpful tools to make planning a breeze.
ParticipantA: That sounds great, I'll definitely check it out. What's the most important thing you've learned from planning your family reunions?
ParticipantB: I think the most important thing is to be flexible. Sometimes things don't go as planned, but as long as we're all together and having fun, it doesn't really matter.
ParticipantA: I totally agree. Flexibility is key. Well, thanks for sharing your experience with me. I really appreciate it.
ParticipantB: Of course, it was my pleasure. Have a great day!
ParticipantA: You too, take care!
